chapter: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
title: Eldon Benge makes him a cornet
summary: The Chicago Symphony's Benge hears him at the Brass Rail and makes a cornet for him, puzzled by improvisation.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: One is a Benge coronet that he, Eldon Alvin Benge made for me. He was the first trumpet player in the Chicago Symphony Orchestra for quite a few years. And he started, was making trumpets. But he heard me play at a place called the 'Brass Rail' in Chicago when I had Peewee Russell and George Brunis, Joe Sullivan, Eddie Condon and Dave Tough on drums. A good band. And Eldon Alvin Benge who was a marvellous musician, first trumpet player with the Chicago Symphony.

BENGE. He heard me play and he just couldn't understand how I could improvise you know. How do you improvise? He could read anything and play anything on the trumpet but he couldn't improvise a note. You have to know your harmony. Have

a good ear and have the feeling for it naturally. Basic rhythm feeling. And know your harmony and know how to improvise. You have to know all your chords on your instrument as well as being able to hear them, you have to have a good ear.

And he could not do that to save his neck. So we got talking and he liked me and I tried to show him how to improvise but he couldn't make it. And I asked him about, you know, I said I don't play trumpet but a cornet. So he made the cornet for me which I took overseas with me. I wasn't in a band, I was in the 462nd AAA Automatic Weapons. Hit Normandy, D plus 4 and lost my patriotism real quick. (LAUGHTER). As I told you before I was....
